name: Yellow Iris
grown_as: The native yellow flag, grown wild at William's pond edge.
habit: Tall clumps of upright sword leaves 60 to 120 cm high in fans from creeping rhizomes in mud or shallow water, with branched flower stems about as tall as the leaves. Spreads into large stands.

leaf.arrangement: In flat fans, each leaf folded at the base and sitting astride the next
leaf.outline: 50 to 90 cm (up to 150 cm) long by 1 to 3 cm wide, narrowing gradually to the tip
leaf.base: Overlapping in the fan, pale or pinkish
leaf.veins: A clear raised midrib down the middle on both faces, with fine parallel veins either side

flower.form: An iris with three broad drooping falls and three small upright standards; no beard
flower.petals: Six tepals: three broad, rounded falls hanging down; three standards, small and narrow, upright, much shorter than the falls. Three yellow, petal-like style arms arch over the falls.
flower.centre: Fine brown-purple veins on each fall round a deeper orange-yellow patch; no beard
flower.behind: A green, leaf-like spathe at the base of each flower
flower.carried: Several flowers on a branched stem, opening one after another, upright

fruit: A large three-sided green capsule 4 to 8 cm, hanging, splitting into three in autumn to show neat stacks of flat brown seeds like piles of coins.
seedling: Not drawn. A narrow sword leaf; spreads mostly by rhizome.
winter: Leaves die back brown and flattened; short green shoots at the base; rhizomes in the mud.

leaf: a long sword-shaped leaf narrowing to a point
a raised midrib down the middle
bloom: three broad drooping yellow falls with fine brown veins
bulb: a thick creeping, branching rhizome in mud, brownish-pink
fans of leaves from its tips and roots beneath
shoots: fans of green sword leaves at the water's edge
each leaf with a raised midrib, the fans in one flat plane
flower: branched stems with bright yellow flowers among the leaves
seedhead: some split open showing stacked brown seeds
dormant: brown dead leaves flattened over the rhizomes
maybe short green shoots at the base

look_alikes: Stinking iris (Iris foetidissima) has dark evergreen leaves, dull purplish or yellowish flowers and orange seeds. Sweet flag (Acorus calamus) has similar leaves with a wavy edge that smell of tangerine when crushed. Bur-reeds have three-sided leaves at the base and spiky ball flowers.
